content: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
author: Viktor Frankl
sourceWork: Yes to Life: In Spite of Everything (1946)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Human beings are never a finished product; we exist in perpetual transit between our basic instincts and our highest potential. The tension we feel inside is not a flaw—it is the very engine of self-evolution.

Across his life and work, Viktor Frankl saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Growing into a fuller version of yourself requires crossing uncertain territory with no safety net. You have to be willing to outgrow the comfort of familiar limitations to step into who you are capable of becoming.
reflectionPrompt: What current difficulty or obstacle are you facing that could become your greatest training ground?
